subject: Acme: Audit logging & SOC 2 follow-up
messages:

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Subject: Acme: Audit logging & SOC 2 follow-up

Hi Alex —

Great to speak earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so your security team has everything in one place. If you want a recorded demo or deeper tech dive, Aditya (security) and David (SRE/solutions) can join.

Summary of Redwood audit logging capabilities (high level):
- Admin activity logs: who performed console actions, user id, IP, timestamp, action type, resource path, request id.
- API request logs: per-request metadata (client id, request id, model id, prompt/response size metrics, token counts, latency, status).
- Exportability: daily/streaming exports in JSON/Parquet to customer S3 buckets; live streaming to Kinesis / PubSub / syslog endpoints or via Fluentd.
- Immutability & retention: append-only storage with retention lock options (WORM-like retention), signed digests for tamper detection, configurable retention policies per-account.
- Access controls & encryption: RBAC for log access, separate audit-log access logs, encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private.
- SIEM integrations: native support for forwarding to Splunk/Datadog/Elastic via syslog or streamed exports.

Compliance posture:
- SOC 2: currently in Type II audit process for our hosted product; expected completion Q2 2026. We can provide the SOC 2 report under NDA once finalized and a SOC 2 readiness packet (attached).
- GDPR: we support a Data Processing Addendum and data subject request tooling; logs can be configured to exclude full prompt text by default to reduce PII surface area.
- HIPAA: BAA available for Dedicated/Private deployments; we can discuss architecture for PHI workflows.

What we can share right away:
- Product sheet (attached) with audit logging features and export examples.
- Sample logs (attached JSON) that show schema and fields.
- SOC 2 readiness packet (attached).

Suggested next steps:
1) I’ll init the security questionnaire in a shared Drive (link below).
2) Schedule a 45-minute security deep-dive with Aditya + David and your security team — suggested Wed 11/18 10:00AM PT.
3) We’ll enable a short trial instance with log export enabled so your team can validate parsing/retention/exports.

Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-acme-security-questionnaire
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567/ACME-EXP-2026-001

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the quick recap and attachments. A few clarifying questions from our security team before the deep-dive:

1) Immutability: can you confirm whether retention lock is enforceable by us (customer) and whether Redwood can administratively override deletes? We need a definite "cannot be changed or deleted by provider" capability for certain retention windows.
2) Log contents: do API logs include full prompt/response text by default? We need to understand PII surface area — ideally the logs would include metadata only unless we opt-in to full transcripts.
3) Export formats: for streaming exports, are the records JSON lines with full schema? Is compression supported?
4) SIEM: do you support secure syslog over TLS or only cloud-streaming endpoints?

We also want to schedule the security deep-dive on Wed 11/18 at 10:00AM PT — can you confirm Aditya and David are available?

Finally, we’d like you to initiate the security questionnaire so our procurement team can start reviewing.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Head of Security Operations
Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Acme: Audit logging & SOC 2 follow-up

Alex — appreciate the detailed questions. Quick answers below; Aditya will add any technical specifics during the deep-dive.

1) Immutability/Retention lock: For hosted customers we offer "retention lock" which prevents deletion for a configured window (e.g., 90/365/ever). For Dedicated/Private we can enable customer-controlled retention locks backed by tenant-isolated storage; administrative overrides are restricted and require documented change requests with audit trails. If you need provider-proof WORM for legal hold we can discuss an architecture using immutable S3 object lock on exported files to your bucket.

2) Log contents & PII: By default API logs capture request/response metadata (token counts, model id, latency, truncated text preview) but do NOT persist full prompt/response bodies unless you opt into full transcript logging. We can provide a redact-on-export option and field-level retention.

3) Export formats & compression: Streaming exports are JSON Lines (one JSON object per event) with optional gzip compression; daily/parquet exports are also supported for analytics workflows.

4) SIEM integrations: We support secure syslog over TLS and native integrations with Splunk and Datadog. Streaming to customer endpoints (Kinesis/GCS PubSub) is supported as well.

We’ll attach a sample log schema (see attached JSON) and a short playbook for enabling exports and retention locks.

Aditya and David — are you available for Wed 11/18 10:00AM PT for a 45-minute session? If so I’ll send the calendar invite and invite the Acme security/infra folks.

Next steps from my side:
- I’ve initialized the security questionnaire and uploaded it to the Drive link below (acme_security_questionnaire.xlsx).
- I’ll enable a short trial with export-to-S3 option turned on so Acme can validate parsing.

Regards,
Marissa
